shipped_rows.title_o: Female facial attractiveness increases during the fertile phase of the menstrual cycle
shipped_rows.authors_o: Roberts; Havlicek; Flegr; Hruskova; Little; Jones; Perrett; Petrie

blind_target.title: Changes in fat distribution (WHR) and body weight across the menstrual cycle.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The objective of the current research was to provide an operational replication of the finding that women’s faces are more attractive at high fertility (Roberts et al., 2004) and of the finding that women’s WHRs are lower at high fertility (Kirchengast and Gartner, 2002).
blind_target.outcome_quote: We designed the current study to replicate two other potential cues of women’s ovulatory status: lower waist-to-hip ratios at high fertility and enhanced facial attractiveness at high fertility. We failed to replicate either effect.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall failure verdict for both designated replication targets.

luna_triage.reason: The paper explicitly operationally replicates the lower-WHR-at-high-fertility finding attributed to Kirchengast and Gartner (2002). The supplied shipped row is Roberts et al. (2004), a distinct facial-attractiveness paper, so it does not represent this target.
luna_triage.omission_quote: The objective of the current research was to provide an operational replication of the finding that women’s faces are more attractive at high fertility (Roberts et al., 2004) and of the finding that women’s WHRs are lower at high fertility (Kirchengast and Gartner, 2002).
luna_triage.identity_quote: Kirchengast, S., and Gartner, M. (2002). Changes in fat distribution (WHR) and body weight across the menstrual cycle. Collegium Anthropologicum, 26 (Suppl), 47-57.
luna_triage.duplicate_quote: Roberts, S. C., Havlicek, J., Flegr, J., Hruskova, M., Little, A. C., Jones, B. C., Perrett, D. I., and Petrie, M. (2004). Female facial attractiveness increases during the fertile phase of the menstrual cycle.

quality_gate: Luna is triage only. Independently establish actual empirical retesting and absence under ALL shipped identities/alternate reports. Read prior objections. No paper outcome is being requested.
